title: Count Complete Subarrays in an Array
summary: Given an array of positive integers, count the number of contiguous subarrays where the count of distinct elements matches the count of distinct elements in the entire array.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, count the number of contiguous subarrays where the count of distinct elements matches the count of distinct elements in the entire array.
constraints: A subarray is complete when it contains every distinct value appearing anywhere in nums.
Count all nonempty contiguous complete subarrays.
hints: Track a frequency map in a right-expanding window.
While the window contains every global distinct value, remove from its left.
After shrinking, left equals the number of valid starts for this right endpoint; add it.
Every earlier start still contains all required values and every later start does not, so exactly left subarrays are counted.
editorial: Every earlier start still contains all required values and every later start does not, so exactly left subarrays are counted.

tests.explanation: Exactly four subarrays contain all three distinct values one, two, and three.
The two singleton subarrays and the full array all contain the sole distinct value.
